title: Anyone have tips for not wasting usage on Codex and Claude?
author: Alarming_Scientist
selftext:
I'm making an isometric post apocalypse game (im on my first 4 days rn and am just making a demo of the first area via godot along with arenas for testing combat) and I realized I'm probably being inefficient as all hell in utilizing usage. 

  
Anyone have tips for not obliterating usage? 

  
Any tips would be much appreciated. 🙏

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body:
Let's say you have a process that the LLM is helping you directly with, let's make something up like, you reorder a folder of data. To do that it will spit it out directly, or even write some temp code (but then throw that code away). Start to have your LLM also make tools that are deterministic regular programs that use no AI where possible. I have something that runs and tests my games in Playwright, it was written with the LLM but doesn't use token to run.

Also, where possible, plan as far as you can in a document, with better models on higher settings. But once you have those very detailed documents on what you want to build, lower models (cheaper) can follow those exact instructions. So high effort to write and design and pre-test the idea. Then once solid use a cheaper model to execute it. Even if you do both on high effort though, planning in a doc first, and then executing in code will use less tokens in general.

comments.author: StellarSoupStudio
comments.body:
Are you using git for version control? Have you implemented a system for levels or as you say "areas" rather than having it all be in a single file? Also this is something you can ask your coding agent, something along the lines of:

What changes to the code base can we make to be more like a proper software project?

And see what it says

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body:
Documentation. Build a solid roadmap. Use it to build a solid blueprint broken into phases. Break each phase into the smallest isolated chunks possible to avoid drift. Always use the same agent to blueprint as you will to build. Never let the machine make decisions. Never let the machine 'one shot prompt' anything (this isn't real). 

Good luck, be well.

comments.author: bigorangemachine
comments.body:
Break up your topics or features.

If you need to tangent something on this thread ... it's better to make a new thread/session.

The issue is the more you put into a session the more expensive it is because you re-count the previous tokens on each message.

Ask it to delegate to a sub agent as well.

replies.author: Reklaw12
replies.body:
Yeah this is the biggest usage killer for people new to agents.

Don't work in one continuous on-going chat. Ask the agent to make sure the skills and project context needed to work on a feature are in place for new instances, then start fresh for every different piece of work.

Avoid continuing long context threads older than an hour too, as the cache will have expired so you have to repay for the whole lot to be loaded again.
Catches a lot of people out when they ask a single question a day later and see 20% of their usage go in one chunk!

comments.author: skill-tap
comments.body: Will the game be played on a device, like Gameboy style, one software instance per user? Scaled to a server with multiple instances? Even at scale, single player or mmorpg style? That should all be well mapped out, in the brief at the start. Even if things won't be implemented until later in development, you want to know what pillars to land things on when you're laying the foundation.

comments.author: kelseyeek
comments.body: The thing that just made a huge difference for me was learning to keep starting new threads instead of continuing long ones, and to give it a set of instructions to, when I give it directions, make a set of plans then spin up sub agents to outsource execution to, while also asking it to evaluate what model of subagent is necessary.  I swear my usage dropped by 80% with those 2 changes.

comments.author: HugoDzz
comments.body:
Something simple and effective is to separate thinking what you want and prompt: take time to write down everything you want (and you want tests for) upfront and prompt to AI only when you are settled on the scope of what you're asking.

That way, improvised back and forth (often with big usage attached) is less likely to happen.
